# Our data {background-color="#dc354a"}

## NHL player stats, 2023–24

One row per player per team, regular season only

```{r, echo = FALSE}
hockey = read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hbdaarstad/NHL-22-24-Season-Data/main/hockey_stats.csv") |>
  filter(!is.na(position), position != "G")

hockey |>
  select(player, team, position, goals, assists, points)
```

::: callout-note
Positions: `C` = center, `L` = left wing, `R` = right wing, `D` = defense. We drop goalies (`G`).
:::

## Google Trends: Montreal Canadiens

Monthly U.S. search interest, 2004 to 2026

```{r, echo = FALSE}
google_trends = read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hbdaarstad/NHL-22-24-Season-Data/main/google_trends.csv") |>
  select(month, montreal_canadiens)

google_trends
```

::: callout-note
Google Trends scores each month 0–100, where 100 = the busiest month in the whole period. It is **not** a count of searches.
:::

## Team goals by position

This one is made for you: each team's total goals by position, plus a `Total` column

```{r, echo = FALSE}
hockey_goals <- hockey |>
  group_by(team, position) |>
  summarise(goals = sum(goals, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = position, values_from = goals, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(-team)))

hockey_goals
```

## Playoff teams

Also made for you: the 16 teams that made the 2024 Stanley Cup playoffs

```{r, echo = TRUE}
playoffs_2024 <- c("FLA", "BOS", "TOR", "TBL", "NYR", "WSH", "CAR", "NYI",
                   "DAL", "VGK", "COL", "WPG", "VAN", "NSH", "EDM", "LAK")
```

# Box plots {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Goals Box Plot 🏒 🚨

Using the `hockey` dataset:

1.  Build a box plot of the number of `goals` scored by all NHL players in the 2023–24 regular season.

2.  Color the outliers and change their shape.

3.  Add a point for the **mean** number of goals.

4.  Add a title, subtitle, and axis labels.

::: callout-tip
1.  Use `aes(x = "", y = goals)` to get a single box

2.  Outliers are set inside `geom_boxplot()` with `outlier.color =`, `outlier.shape =`, `outlier.size =`

3.  To add the mean: `stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point")`
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 5L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 Goals Box Plot Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

ggplot(data = hockey, aes(y = "", x = goals)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    alpha = 0.7,                       # transparency of the box fill
    outlier.color = "cornflowerblue",  # color of outlier points
    outlier.shape = 8,                 # outlier symbol is a star
    outlier.size = 1                   # outlier size
  ) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point",
               shape = 20, size = 4, color = "coral") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Regular Season Goals by Player",
       subtitle = "NHL 2023–24",
       x = "",
       y = "Goals Scored") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

::: notes
The mean sits above the median: a few big scorers pull the mean up (right-skewed)
:::

# Multiple box plots {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Team Goals by Position 🏒 🚨

What **percent** of each team's goals comes from each position?

Using `hockey_goals`:

1.  Make a new object called `hockey_boxplot` with the percent of goals from each position: `rw_percent`, `lw_percent`, `c_percent`, `d_percent`.

2.  Make a box plot for each position and combine them with `patchwork`.

::: callout-tip
1.  Percent = the position's goals divided by `Total`, times 100. Use `mutate()`

2.  Combine plots with `+` and set the layout with `plot_layout(ncol = 4)`
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 7L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 Team Goals by Position Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

Step 1: the percentages

```{r}
#| echo: true

hockey_boxplot <- hockey_goals |>
  mutate(
    rw_percent = R / Total * 100,
    lw_percent = L / Total * 100,
    c_percent  = C / Total * 100,
    d_percent  = D / Total * 100
  )

hockey_boxplot
```

## 🚨 🏒 Team Goals by Position Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

Step 2: plot

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

rw <- ggplot(hockey_boxplot, aes(x = "", y = rw_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Right Wing", y = "% of Team Goals")

lw <- ggplot(hockey_boxplot, aes(x = "", y = lw_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Left Wing", y = NULL)

cen <- ggplot(hockey_boxplot, aes(x = "", y = c_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Center", y = NULL)

d <- ggplot(hockey_boxplot, aes(x = "", y = d_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Defense", y = NULL)

rw + lw + cen + d +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Boxplots of the Percentage of Goals Scored",
    subtitle = "by Position Across all NHL Teams",
    caption = "NHL Regular Season 2023–24"
  ) & scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
```

# Time series {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Canadians Searches 🏒 🚨

Using the `google_trends` dataset:

1.  Make a time series plot of the Google search score for the Montreal Canadians (`montreal_canadiens`) by `month`, 2004 to 2026.

2.  Label the x-axis every 2 years.

3.  Add a trend line and a dashed line at the average score.

4.  Add a title, subtitle, axis labels, and a caption.

::: callout-tip
1.  Connect the points with `geom_line()`

2.  `scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y")`

3.  Trend line: `geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE)`. Average: `geom_hline(yintercept = mean(...), linetype = 2)`
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 6.5L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 Canadians Searches Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

ggplot(google_trends, aes(x = month, y = montreal_canadiens)) +
  geom_line(color = "coral2") +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE,
              color = "grey40", linewidth = .5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(google_trends$montreal_canadiens, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "U.S. Google searches for the Montreal Canadiens spike each spring",
       subtitle = "Monthly Google Trends interest, January 2004 to October 2026",
       y = "Search interest (0–100)", x = "Month",
       caption = "Source: Google Trends") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14))
```

::: notes
The biggest spikes are playoff runs: May 2010, May 2014, June 2021 (Stanley Cup Final), May 2026
:::

### How do we add a line for the playoff runs? 🏒

```{r, echo = TRUE}

ggplot(google_trends, aes(x = month, y = montreal_canadiens)) +
  geom_line(color = "coral2") +
  geom_smooth(method = lm, se = FALSE,
              color = "grey40", linewidth = .5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(google_trends$montreal_canadiens, na.rm = TRUE),
             linetype = 2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date(c("2010-05-01", "2014-05-01",
                                    "2021-06-01", "2026-05-01")),
             linetype = 2) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "2 years", date_labels = "%Y") +
  labs(title = "U.S. Google searches for the Montreal Canadians spike each spring",
       subtitle = "Monthly Google Trends interest, January 2004 to October 2026",
       y = "Search interest (0–100)", x = "Month",
       caption = "Source: Google Trends") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1, size = 9),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14))


```

# Creating a new variable {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Playoff Teams 🏒 🚨

Using `hockey_boxplot` and the `playoffs_2024` list:

1.  Make a new variable called `playoffs` that is `"Clinched"` if the team made the playoffs and `"Eliminated"` if it did not.

2.  Store it as a new object called `hockey_newvar`.

::: callout-tip
1.  `case_when()` goes **inside** `mutate()`

2.  `%in%` checks whether a value is in a list: `team %in% playoffs_2024`

3.  There is no `!%in%`. For "not in", use `!(team %in% playoffs_2024)`
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 4L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 Playoff Teams Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true

hockey_newvar <- hockey_boxplot |>
  mutate(playoffs = case_when(
    team %in% playoffs_2024 ~ "Clinched",
    !(team %in% playoffs_2024) ~ "Eliminated"
  ))

head(hockey_newvar)
```

::: callout-tip
You can also write the last line as `TRUE ~ "Eliminated"`. `TRUE ~` means "everything else."
:::

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 Graphing the New Variable 🏒 🚨

1.  Keep only the teams that **clinched** the playoffs.

2.  Build box plots of the percent of goals by position for those teams, like before.

::: callout-tip
1.  Use `filter(playoffs == "Clinched")`

2.  You can copy your box plot code from earlier: just change the data!
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 5L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 Graphing the New Variable Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

hockey_clinched <- hockey_newvar |>
  filter(playoffs == "Clinched")

rw <- ggplot(hockey_clinched, aes(x = "", y = rw_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Right Wing", y = "% of Team Goals")

lw <- ggplot(hockey_clinched, aes(x = "", y = lw_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Left Wing", y = NULL)

cen <- ggplot(hockey_clinched, aes(x = "", y = c_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Center", y = NULL)

d <- ggplot(hockey_clinched, aes(x = "", y = d_percent)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "gray", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Defense", y = NULL)

rw + lw + cen + d +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Boxplots of the Percentage of Goals Scored",
    subtitle = "by Position across NHL Teams who Clinched the Playoffs",
    caption = "NHL Regular Season 2023–24"
  ) & scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100))
```

## 🚨 🏒 Graphing the New Variable Adv. Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

Compare clinched **and** eliminated teams in one plot

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column

rink_colors <- c("Clinched" = "#0A9396", "Eliminated" = "#BB3E03")

hockey_newvar |>
  pivot_longer(c(rw_percent, lw_percent, c_percent, d_percent),
               names_to = "position", values_to = "percent") |>
  mutate(position = factor(position,
    levels = c("rw_percent", "lw_percent", "c_percent", "d_percent"),
    labels = c("Right Wing", "Left Wing", "Center", "Defense"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = position, y = percent, fill = playoffs)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rink_colors, name = "Playoffs") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Position", y = "% of Team Goals",
       title = "Percentage of Goals Scored by Position",
       subtitle = "Playoff vs. non-playoff teams",
       caption = "NHL Regular Season 2023–24") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# t-tests {background-color="#dc354a"}

## 🚨 Your turn: 🏒 t-test 🏒 🚨

Using `hockey_newvar`:

1.  Test whether teams that made the playoffs scored more **total goals** (`Total`) than teams that did not.

2.  Make a new variable `offense_perct`: the percent of goals from forwards (right wing + left wing + center).

3.  Test whether playoff teams get a different percent of their goals from **defense** (`d_percent`).

4.  Which differences are statistically significant?

::: callout-tip
1.  The formula is `t.test(OUTCOME ~ GROUP, data = DATA)`

2.  A difference is statistically significant if the **p-value** is less than 0.05
:::

```{r}
countdown::countdown(minutes = 6.5L)
```

## 🚨 🏒 t-test Code Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

t.test(Total ~ playoffs, data = hockey_newvar)

hockey_ttest <- hockey_newvar |>
  mutate(offense_perct = rw_percent + lw_percent + c_percent)

t.test(d_percent ~ playoffs, data = hockey_ttest)
```

## 🚨 🏒 t-test Answer 🏒 🚨 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: column

t.test(Total ~ playoffs, data = hockey_newvar)

hockey_ttest <- hockey_newvar |>
  mutate(offense_perct = rw_percent + lw_percent + c_percent)

t.test(d_percent ~ playoffs, data = hockey_ttest)
```

. . .

**Total goals**: playoff teams scored about 269 goals vs. 232, p = 0.0004: **significant**

. . .

**Defense share**: p = 0.15: **not** significant

. . .

::: callout-note
`offense_perct` and `d_percent` always add up to 100, so testing `offense_perct` gives the same p-value
:::
